sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Ádammair is an Irish god. He is the husband of the Irish woodland goddess Flidais. He is obscure in comparison to his famous consort. He has few known myths of his own. Flidais was a goddess of wild animals and the hunt. She rode in a chariot drawn by deer. In some accounts Ádammair is called a fairy. Nothing else is known about him beyond his marriage to the goddess. His name survives mainly through his connection to Flidais.
objective: This article establishes Ádammair as the obscure Irish god husband of the woodland goddess Flidais.
